newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller criticises Saddam aggression.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller criticises Saddam aggression.

text.p: Turkish foreign minister Tansu Ciller criticised the Iraqi aggression in Kurdish-controlled northern Iraq that led to U.S. air strikes on southern Iraq on Tuesday.
"The fact that (Iraqi President) Saddam Hussein and his forces were involved in an action that is against the United Nations decisions has bothered us and it has worried us," Ciller told Reuters.
"We never supported Saddam's aggression and we will not be supporting it at any time. We have always made that very clear."

Ciller said Turkey had tried very hard through diplomatic means to allay the need for the strike, but that she had learned through a telephone call with U.S. President Bill Clinton early on Tuesday that efforts had been in vain.
"According to information I received from President Clinton, the situation has taken on a new dimension with America's intervention against 16 targets," she told reporters.
On Tuesday the United States said it had launched cruise missile attacks against Iraq in retaliation for the Iraqi attacks.

Ciller said she had told Clinton that the operation should not hurt Turkey's fight with its own rebel Kurds in the southeast of the country. The fight between the army and separatist Kurds seeking control of southeast Turkey has claimed more than 20,000 lives in the past 12 years.
Ciller on Tuesday postponed her planned trip to Jordan because of the crisis in Iraq.
Saddam's troops moved into the northern Iraqi city of Arbil on Saturday in support of a Kurdish group battling another Kurdish faction. Iraq has since said it would withdraw its troops.
